Built from durable materials and designed for everyday use, Kingston widespread bathroom faucets offer reliable performance and timeless appeal. What Is a Widespread Bathroom Faucet? A widespread bathroom faucet has three separate pieces: a spout and two handles. Each piece is installed individually through separate holes in the sink or countertop. Unlike a centerset faucet, the handles and spout are not connected to a single base. This creates a more open and custom look. Most widespread faucets fit sinks with hole spacing between 8 and 16 inches. They are commonly used on larger vanities in primary bathrooms, guest bathrooms, and powder rooms. Why Choose a Widespread Faucet? Widespread faucets remain one of the most popular bathroom faucet styles. They offer flexible installation, lasting performance, and a custom look. Elegant Appearance The separate handles create a clean and balanced look. Many homeowners choose widespread faucets because they create a more custom look. Flexible Installation The handles can be installed farther apart than a standard centerset faucet. This flexibility allows for a more custom setup and works well with many sink styles. Many Design Options Widespread faucets are available in traditional, transitional, and modern designs. No matter your bathroom style, there is a faucet that can match it. Durable Performance Many widespread faucets feature solid brass construction and ceramic disc cartridges. Solid brass is strong and durable, while ceramic disc cartridges help prevent leaks and keep the faucet working smoothly. How to Know If Your Sink Is Compatible Before purchasing a new faucet, check your sink's hole spacing. Measure from the center of the left hole to the center of the right hole. If the measurement is between 8 and 16 inches, your sink is designed for a widespread faucet. If your sink has only one hole or a 4-inch centerset layout, you may need a different faucet style. Measuring your sink first can help you choose the right faucet. Popular Widespread Faucet Finishes The finish you choose plays a big role in your bathroom's overall style. Some finishes create a bold statement, while others offer a more classic appearance. Matte Black Matte Black remains one of the most popular choices for modern bathrooms. It creates strong contrast and works well with white vanities, stone countertops, and light-colored tile. Brushed Nickel Brushed Nickel has a soft, warm appearance. It is also good at hiding fingerprints and water spots, making it a practical option for busy bathrooms. Polished Chrome Polished Chrome offers a bright, reflective finish that never goes out of style. It pairs well with both traditional and contemporary designs. Oil Rubbed Bronze Oil Rubbed Bronze adds warmth and character. It is often used in farmhouse, rustic, and traditional bathrooms. Brass Brass finishes have become increasingly popular in recent years. Their warm color adds character and creates an eye-catching look. Not sure which finish is right for your bathroom? Check out The Best Finishes for Widespread Bathroom Faucets for ideas, comparisons, and design tips. Looking for a Smaller Widespread Faucet? Not every bathroom has a large vanity. Mini widespread bathroom faucets offer the same stylish look as standard widespread faucets but take up less space. They are a great choice for guest bathrooms, powder rooms, and smaller vanities. If you're considering a compact faucet, explore our guide, The 10 Best Mini Widespread Bathroom Faucets. The guide features popular mini widespread faucets and ideas for smaller bathrooms. Lever Handles vs. Cross Handles Handle style can have a big impact on the overall design of your faucet. Lever Handles Lever handles have a simple and modern appearance. They are easy to use and work well in contemporary and transitional bathrooms. Cross Handles Cross handles offer a more traditional look. They are often chosen for vintage, farmhouse, and classic bathroom designs. Both options provide reliable performance. The right choice depends on your personal style. Water Efficiency and Everyday Performance Today's widespread faucets do more than look good. Many faucets are designed to use less water while still providing strong performance. WaterSense-certified faucets can help save water while maintaining good water flow. Many faucets also include ceramic disc cartridges. These cartridges help prevent drips and keep the faucet operating smoothly over time. Installation and Maintenance Widespread faucets can be installed by experienced DIY homeowners or professional plumbers. Before installation, confirm that your sink has the correct hole spacing. You should also make sure the faucet works with your sink drain. Routine maintenance is simple. Cleaning the aerator from time to time can help keep the faucet performing well.
